title: fix(sse): robust chunking/framing for streaming partial JSON and delimiter ordering
author: Ethan Chen
description: Context: Customers and internal e2e tests exposed intermittent JSON parse errors in streaming responses when the server emitted partial JSON fragments in SSE chunks. Problems observed: (1) missing/newline delimiter ordering causing clients that parse 'data:' frames to see truncated JSON objects, (2) function_call and structured tokens being emitted out-of-order relative to event boundaries, and (3) the OpenAI-compat adapter sometimes emitting multiple small events without proper 'data: ' delimiters which broke a few third-party SSE parsers. Motivation: Streaming stability is critical for hosted API and OpenAI-compatible clients; small framing bugs lead to client-side failures or degraded UX for tool/function calling and structured outputs. Changes made: - Introduced a small framing utility (frame_util.go) that centralizes SSE chunk assembly and enforces: always emit a newline-terminated 'data: ' line per logical event, coalesce partial token fragments into a reassembly buffer, and only flush when an event boundary is reached or a configured max-chunk-size is hit. - Reworked streamer pipeline (streamer.go) to use the framing util; ensured KV-cache and batch flush hooks don't split JSON tokens across frames. - Fixed the OpenAI compatibility adapter (openai/compat/stream_adapter.go) to consume framed events from the new util and to guarantee the correct ordering for 'delta' / 'function_call' token emission. Also ensure the final [DONE] event is sent after all token events and with correct delimiter format. - Updated JS streaming client example (sdk/js/stream-client.js) to be tolerant of small chunking differences (reassembly example) and added a note in the streaming guide. - Added unit tests for: partial JSON reassembly, delimiter ordering, and function_call token ordering. - Added integration/e2e tests that exercise the end-to-end OpenAI-compat streaming path under throttled network conditions to reproduce previous failures. Commits: - 8a2f3b7: introduce frame_util and initial tests - b341e20: refactor streamer to use frame_util, prevent mid-token flushes - c9f1d45: adapt openai compat adapter to new framing contract - d0e6f9a: update js example and docs + add e2e tests - 1f3c927: test cleanup and CI flakiness fixes Files changed (high-level): - server/sse/frame_util.go (new) - server/sse/streamer.go (modified) - openai/compat/stream_adapter.go (modified) - sdk/js/stream-client.js (modified example) - docs/api/streaming.md (modified) - tests/unit/streaming/partial_reassembly_test.go (new) - tests/integration/streaming/e2e_throttled_network_test.go (new) - tests/ci/scripts/stream_ci_setup.sh (modified) Review notes and thread summary: - Maya: flagged an issue where frame_util could increase latency by holding partial buffers too long; asked for a max-hold-time fallback. - Author: added a max-hold-time config (default 10ms) and a unit test to validate flush-on-timeout. - Arjun: requested clearer invariants in comments and a small benchmark to prove no measurable regression at 99th percentile; author added microbench and annotated key paths. - Sofia: found an edge case where an empty 'delta' would lead to sending an empty JSON object; author amended the filter to drop empty deltas. CI and rollout: - Initial CI run had two flaky tests failing in the e2e harness (network simulation timeout). Fixed by increasing the harness timeout and adding retry logic for the flaky network emulator start. - Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, race). - Canary rollout: deployed to dedicated-canary (3 hosts) for 24h; monitored per-token latency and error-rate dashboards. Result: no increase in 99th latency, error-rate for streaming JSON parse errors dropped to 0 in canary. Compatibility considerations: - No public API changes. The OpenAI-compat layer behaviour is now more strict about delimiters (but still backwards compatible). - This fixes several observed client breakages (listed in linked_linear). Testing and QA: - Manual verification with the Node SDK example and curl-based SSE consumers. - End-to-end tests added to CI to prevent regressions. - QA checklist completed (unit, integration, doc update, canary). Release notes: "Fix: more robust SSE streaming framing to avoid partial-JSON and delimiter ordering issues that caused client-side parse errors. Improved OpenAI-compat streaming adapter ordering for function_call and structured outputs. Includes tests and doc updates." Additional context: This PR is intentionally conservative: it centralizes framing logic into a single util to reduce duplication and future regressions. Follow-ups: - Consider exposing a tunable for max-chunk-size and max-hold-time per-tenant in Dedicated/private for fine-grained perf tuning. - Investigate streaming telemetry to surface partial-frame counts in Console (ENG-4890).
release_notes: Fix: robust SSE streaming framing to prevent partial-JSON parse errors in streaming responses; OpenAI-compat adapter ordering fixes for function_call and structured output (no breaking API changes).
